newsitem.title: USA: US semiconductor equipment August book-to-bill off.
newsitem.headline: US semiconductor equipment August book-to-bill off.

text.p: The North American semiconductor equipment industry posted a book-to-bill ratio of 0.72 for August, Semiconductor Equipment and Materials International (SEMI) said.
It said the August ratio compared with a revised ratio of 0.76 for July.
The August ratio means that $72 in orders were received for each $100 worth of products shipped.

The SEMI report said that orders received from worldwide customers by North American semiconductor equipment manufacturers in August were $902.7 million, down nine percent from July and down 18 percent from August 1995. During the same period, capital equipment shipments to worldwide customers totaled $1.25 billion, down four percent from the revised July results but 19 percent higher than August 1995.
"The semiconductor market is still working off excess DRAM inventory," Elizabeth Schumann, a senior market analyst for SEMI said in a statement.

"However, most computer market analysts are saying that Christmas 1996 for computers is looking much better than last year, so we expect the semiconductor market, in units at least, to strengthen in the next couple of quarters."
